chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about entering the Ka'bah. He said: 'Entering it is entering into the mercy of Allah, and exiting from it is exiting from sins. He is protected for the remainder of his life, and forgiven for what preceded of his sins.'

key_terms.مَعْصُومٌ: Protected/Infallible (in context of protection from sin)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual meaning of entering and exiting the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the Ka'bah as a locus of divine mercy and spiritual purification, where entry signifies immersion in Allah's grace and exit represents the expiation of past sins. This tradition underscores the concept of *al-ma'sum* (protected from major sins) for the duration of one's life following this act, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Ka'bah not merely as a physical structure but as a metaphysical gateway to forgiveness. The narration highlights the transformative power of the pilgrimage experience, aligning with the broader theological view of the Ka'bah as the 'Umm al-Qura' (Mother of Cities) and the center of spiritual gravity for believers.
